The model flagged this applicant as high‑risk because two of the three key signals push the default probability upward, outweighing the one factor that pulls it down.  

First, the applicant has one recent 30‑to‑59‑day past‑due payment. That single late payment adds a noticeable amount to the risk score, indicating a recent slip in repayment behavior.  

Second, the applicant holds a large number of open credit lines—20 in total. Having many active accounts raises the model’s concern that the borrower may be over‑extended, adding further risk.  

The only mitigating element is the debt‑to‑income figure, which, at the observed level, actually reduces risk a bit. However, the combined effect of the late payment and many open accounts is strong enough that the model still classifies the applicant as a 50 % chance of default, i.e., high risk.
